full_judgment:
II. Independent witnesses who are close neighbors of convict-appellant had not been examined in support of prosecution case and adverse presumption under section 114(g) of The Evidence Act has arisen against the prosecution. 

 23. Contention Nos. 2 and 3: Contention Nos. 2 and 3 are dealt with together. It has been contended that PW 6 in his evidence stated that as many as six families live in the place of occurrence and none of the persons of those families had been examined and Sunil Kumar Sen, charge- sheet witness No. 11 and Chowkidar whose name had been disclosed by PW 6 as identifier of the house of convict-appellant had not been, also, examined and non-examination of close door neighbours and Sunil Kumar Sen call for an adverse presumption under section 114(g) of The Evidence Act. 

 24. Section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, 1872 postulates that non-examination of independent witness raises a presumption against prosecution case. 

 26. In First Information Report it is stated that Sub-Inspector Sunil Kumar Sen who figured as charge-sheet witness No. 11 accompanied Sub-Inspector of Police PW 1 and, also, PW 6 to the place of occurrence and apprehended convict- appellant. PW 6 in his testimony testified that local chowkider took them to the place of occurrence but these two persons had not been placed in witness box by prosecution. No explanation even had been even assigned for their non-examination by prosecution. Non-production of above two witnesses was very much fatal for prosecution case and the presumption contemplated in section 114(g) of The Evidence Act must follow.
